name: FarmFlow
whatItIs: A real-time decision-support platform for greenhouse & high-value crop growers — live sensor telemetry, a streaming AI crop advisor, remote actuator control and a moderated grower community.
description: A real-time greenhouse control & AI advisory platform fusing live ESP32 sensor data, soil composition and weather forecasts into crop-specific guidance.
detailedDescription: FarmFlow is a real-time decision-support platform for greenhouse and high-value crop growers. ESP32 nodes (temp/humidity, light and soil-moisture sensors, plus servo/stepper/motor actuators) publish over MQTT to HiveMQ Cloud, feeding an Express 5 + Socket.IO API that writes into a native MongoDB time-series collection. Every advisory card fuses three sources concurrently — the field's live sensor reading, ISRIC SoilGrids soil composition and the Open-Meteo forecast — into one prompt for a streaming AI advisor, which escalates to a verified human agronomist when a case needs it. A Next.js 16 client renders the live charts, actuator controls, map-based field setup and an AI-moderated grower forum. The whole stack is self-hosted on a VPS behind Cloudflare and Caddy, with Tailscale gating all administrative and CI/CD access.
motive: 🌾 Greenhouse growers had no real-time visibility into their own fields' sensor data
🧭 Wanted crop advice grounded in real sensor, soil & weather data instead of generic tips
🩺 Aimed to blend a fast AI answer with human expert escalation for the cases that matter
architecture: 🧩 ESP32 nodes (or the ESP-Simulator) publish sensor + actuator data over MQTT (TLS) to HiveMQ Cloud
🗄️ Express 5 + Socket.IO API ingests readings into a native MongoDB time-series collection (metaField-indexed, 90-day TTL)
🌦️ Live sensor readings, ISRIC SoilGrids soil composition and Open-Meteo forecasts are fetched concurrently and fused into one AI advisory prompt
📡 Next.js 16 client subscribes over an authenticated Socket.IO namespace for live charts and streaming advisor replies
🔒 Deployed behind Cloudflare → Caddy → Docker containers on a VPS reachable only via Tailscale
problemsSolved: 🐛 InfluxDB modeled farmerId/fieldId as unindexed fields, forcing full scans → migrated to native MongoDB time-series with indexed metaField tags
🔌 Frozen ESP32 firmware sends hardware labels, not field IDs → added a short-TTL registry resolving label → field so orphan readings get dropped
🖼️ OpenRouter refused to fetch attachment images from private/localhost URLs → switched to short-lived signed S3 URLs
📖 Offset pagination on a newest-first feed shifted under the reader between requests → switched to (createdAt, _id) cursor paging
🧱 Follower arrays risked hitting MongoDB's 16MB document cap → modeled follows as unique-indexed edge documents instead

name: FineMed
whatItIs: A secure e-commerce platform for buying medicines online with prescription verification.
description: An e-commerce platform for purchasing medicines with secure authentication and prescription verification.
detailedDescription: FineMed is a comprehensive e-commerce platform designed to facilitate the purchase of medicines online. It features a robust user authentication system using JWT and bcrypt, ensuring secure access for customers and admins. Users can browse and search for medicines by name, category, or symptoms, with detailed product pages providing essential information like price, stock availability, and prescription requirements. The platform includes a shopping cart and checkout system with prescription upload functionality for restricted medicines. Admins have access to a dashboard to manage medicines, orders, and prescription verifications. The application integrates secure payment gateways (Stripe/ShurjoPay) and is fully responsive for seamless use across devices.
motive: 🩺 Pharmacies nearby had no easy way for customers to check medicine stock before visiting
🔐 Wanted to practice building a platform that safely handles prescription-restricted purchases
📈 Aimed to learn end-to-end e-commerce flow: cart, checkout and admin order management
architecture: 🧩 Next.js frontend with server components for fast product listing pages
🗄️ Express + MongoDB backend exposing a REST API for products, orders & prescriptions
🔑 JWT-based auth with role separation between customer and admin
☁️ Prescription files uploaded to cloud storage and linked to orders for admin review
problemsSolved: 🐛 Race condition on stock count during checkout → fixed with atomic MongoDB updates
🖼️ Slow image loads on product grid → solved with lazy loading and optimized image sizes
🔁 Duplicate orders on double-click checkout → added request debouncing + idempotency check

name: Bicycle Store
whatItIs: A role-based e-commerce app for browsing and buying bicycles online.
description: A responsive bicycle e-commerce app with role-based authentication and product management.
detailedDescription: Bicycle Store is a feature-rich e-commerce application tailored for bicycle enthusiasts. It offers secure user registration and login with JWT-based authentication and hashed passwords. The platform showcases featured products and allows users to search and filter bicycles by brand, price, or category. Detailed product pages provide specifications and a seamless checkout process with payment integration (SurjoPay/Stripe). The app includes role-based dashboards: customers can view order history and manage profiles, while admins can perform CRUD operations on products and orders. The responsive design ensures a consistent experience across devices, with loading states and user-friendly error handling enhancing usability.
motive: 🚲 Wanted to build a niche-store experience instead of a generic e-commerce template
🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Practice role-based access control between customers and admins
💳 Explore integrating a real regional payment gateway (SurjoPay)
architecture: 🧩 Next.js frontend consuming a REST API for products, carts and orders
🗄️ Express + MongoDB backend with Mongoose schemas for products & orders
🔑 Role-based JWT middleware guarding admin-only routes
💳 Payment gateway integration handled server-side with webhook confirmation
problemsSolved: 🐛 Filter + pagination combo returned stale results → fixed query key caching
🔒 Admin routes were reachable by manipulating client state → enforced server-side role checks
📱 Layout broke on smaller tablets → reworked grid breakpoints for the product listing

name: Events Hub
whatItIs: An event management enterprise platform connecting customers, vendors and admins.
description: An event management enterprise website with admin, customer, vendor features
keyFeatures: Authentication based on customers, admins, vendors
Browse event suggestions based on need
detailedDescription: An event management enterprise website which caters interactive ways of communication and management of event activities incorporating bookings, vendors, suggestions etc
motive: 🎉 Event planning involves too many disconnected calls between customers and vendors
🤝 Wanted one hub where vendors, customers and admins can coordinate in one place
🤖 Curious to experiment with AI-driven event suggestions based on user needs
architecture: 🧩 React frontend with role-specific dashboards for customer, vendor & admin
🗄️ Express + MongoDB backend modeling events, bookings and vendor profiles
🔥 Firebase used for authentication and real-time notifications
🤖 AI suggestion module calling an external model to recommend vendors/events
problemsSolved: 🐛 Vendor availability conflicts when double-booked → added booking-slot locking
📧 Emails landing in spam → fixed with proper SPF/DKIM mail configuration
⚙️ Still under active development — dashboard permissions being refined

name: Aura
whatItIs: An artwork-focused e-commerce platform where artists showcase and sell their creations.
description: An artwork-based unique and beautiful e-commerce platform for artists to showcase and sell their creations.
keyFeatures: User pannel for own arts management
detailedDescription: Aura is an artwork-focused e-commerce platform that empowers artists to showcase and sell their creations to a global audience. The platform features secure user authentication and registration powered by Firebase, enabling both artists and buyers to access personalized features. Users can browse through curated artwork collections, search for specific pieces, and view detailed pages with artist information, descriptions, and pricing. The cart system allows users to add artworks, review total costs, and proceed to a checkout page with a dummy payment gateway for demonstration purposes. An admin panel provides tools to manage artworks, update site content, and handle user requests. Built with a modern tech stack, Aura ensures a responsive and intuitive user experience across devices.
motive: 🎨 Independent artists often lack an affordable, dedicated storefront online
🖼️ Wanted to design a visually distinctive UI instead of a generic product grid
🧪 Used this project to experiment with Firebase auth + hosting end-to-end
architecture: 🧩 React frontend with a gallery-style layout for browsing artworks
🗄️ Express + MongoDB backend storing artwork, artist & order data
🔥 Firebase handling authentication and static hosting
💳 Dummy payment gateway simulating checkout for demo purposes
problemsSolved: 🐛 Large artwork images slowed page load → added responsive image sizing & compression
🔍 Search felt sluggish with many listings → added debounced search input
🎨 Generic template look → reworked layout with a custom gallery grid for visual identity
